document.abstract: The following group of medical papers is assembled for the Journal from the papers programs of the Society's 98th (Fall 1965) and 99th (Spring 1966) Technical Conferences. The Society's strong attention to this subject appears to have started with a breakthrough in 1960 when the subject was included in the sessions of the Fifth International Congress on High-Speed Photography. The Society's meetings and Journal have long welcomed the interests of medical cinematography, cineradiography, etc., but only in recent years has there been a sustained effort for effective integration of the medical sciences and research with photography in SMPTE programs. At the 94th Conference (Fall 1963) in Boston, there were three complete sessions of medical papers, films and lectures; from these sessions and sessions of the 95th, 96th and 97th Conferences have come two groups of papers already published. These groups of papers emphasize the great advances in the application of photography, television technology and allied arts to medical science. Our thanks go to the large group of medical men and their sponsors for these presentations describing their accomplishments and concerns.—Roxanne O'Mally Ray
